title: Evidence Ingestion & SIEM Export Runbook — RBAC v2 + Audit Streams
summary: Working runbook for automating audit-evidence ingestion and SIEM export, aligned to SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls. Focuses on RBAC v2 impacts on log generation/access, the audit log schema baseline, secure export to SIEM (ECS/JSON), and concrete remediation steps to close gaps identified during the Q3 readiness review.
scope: Applies to hosted API, Dedicated clusters, and Private deployment control planes. Covers system-generated audit events (authn/authz, token operations, config changes, rollout events), log transport, retention, integrity verification, and evidence packaging for external auditors. Does NOT include application-level business logs or customer PII extraction flows.
evidence_mapping: SOC2 CC6/CC7 -> immutable-audit-store (S3 immutable bucket + object-lock) : proof = signed-manifest + sha256 checksums
ISO27001 A.12.4 -> audit_log_stream : fields mapped for retention and access reviews
RBAC v2 -> privileged-role-change events : evidence = role_change_audit, approver_id, request_id, before_after_diff
Access Reviews -> evidence = periodic_certification_reports (csv export), membership snapshots
SIEM Exports -> evidence = daily-export-manifests + delivery receipts (Kafka offset/connector commit logs)
rbac_gap_findings: Roles are still coarse-grained for several internal tools (engineering-admin vs platform-operator) — violates least-privilege principle
No automated periodic certification for RBAC v2 roles; current process is ad-hoc and spreadsheet-driven
Audit trails for role-assignment via LDAP/SSO sync are incomplete (missing before-state for bulk imports)
Service accounts lack clear owner tagging, making separation-of-duties attestations harder
Private deployments (customer-managed) do not emit standardized audit streams back to control plane for evidence collection
audit_log_schema_notes: Baseline fields (required): timestamp (ISO8601), event_type, principal_id, principal_type (user/service), action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (success/failure), request_id, session_id, auth_method, source_ip, region, model_version(optional), route
Optional/contextual: user_agent, request_payload_hash, response_status, latency_ms, telemetry_flags
Immutable identifiers: each event MUST include a UUIDv4 request_id and monotonic sequence for a session where applicable
Schema versioning: include schema_version major.minor on each event to allow consumer evolution
PII considerations: do NOT emit raw prompt text in hosted logs unless flagged for retention; if needed use prompt_snippet_hash and store full prompt in encrypted evidence store with access controls
siem_export_requirements: Preferred format: ECS-aligned JSON (mapping docs in linked_artifacts) delivered in daily ndjson batches or streaming via Kafka connector
Encryption: TLS 1.2+ in transit to SIEM; payloads signed using platform signing key (KMS-managed) with manifest containing SHA256 checksums
Retention & Rotation: daily exports retained for 90 days in 'staging' and immutable archive for 7 years as required by compliance (configurable per customer tier)
Redaction: PII redaction policy executed at export boundary; redaction rules stored as versioned config and logged as transformation events
Delivery Guarantees: at-least-once via Kafka + consumer offsets; export manifests must include start/end offsets and record counts for reconciliation
Audit of access: all reads of historical exported evidence must themselves be logged to the immutable store
evidence_automation_design: Producer: microservices and control plane emit structured audit events to central Kafka topic 'audit.events.v2' (schema-validated at producer)
Pre-ingest validation: sidecar lambda validates schema_version, required fields, and rejects malformed events (DLQ -> security-team)
Storage path: validated events written to encrypted S3 staging (partitioned by date/service) with object-lock enabled
Manifesting: nightly batch job creates signed-manifest (json) enumerating objects, counts, sha256 checksums. Manifest published to manifests/ and to Confluence evidence index via webhook
SIEM connector: Kafka Connect or S3 Connector streams ECS-mapped ndjson to SIEM; connector commits feed into daily-manifest for reconciliation
Integrity: periodic background job re-computes checksums and writes signed attestations to the evidence index; automated alerts on mismatch
For Private deployments: lightweight agent ships only metadata (hashes, manifests); customers can choose to forward full logs to our collector if contractual

auditor_q_and_a: Q: Where are audit logs stored and for how long? A: Primary staging in encrypted S3 (90 days), immutable archive with object-lock (7 years by default). Storage locations and retention configurable per customer SLA.

Q: How do you prove integrity of logs to an auditor? A: We publish signed manifests (KMS-signed) with per-object sha256 and maintain a checksum attestation ledger. Integrity jobs re-hash objects and record results to the ledger.

Q: How is access to audit evidence controlled? A: Access governed by RBAC v2; evidence buckets have IAM policies that only allow security-and-compliance roles to list/get; reads are logged and require privileged approval for export.

Q: Do exported SIEM feeds contain PII or prompt text? A: No raw prompt text is exported by default. Any sensitive data is redacted at the export boundary; full prompts are stored only in encrypted evidence store with strict access controls.

Q: How do you handle customer-managed/private deployments? A: We provide an agent that collects metadata and manifests; customer can opt-in to forward full audit streams to our collector under contract. We document the minimal evidence set for audits.

Q: What monitoring/alerting exist for evidence pipeline failures? A: SLIs: ingestion success rate, manifest reconciliation mismatch rate, DLQ size. Alerts routed to sec-oncall and infra-pager with runbooks linked in linked_artifacts.
